# Finite two-colour graph Ramsey theory: the Erdős–Szekeres recursion and the binomial bound

This file develops finite two-colour graph Ramsey theory through the classical
Erdős–Szekeres recursion `R(s+1, t+1) ≤ R(s, t+1) + R(s+1, t)` and the binomial
upper bound `R(s+1, t+1) ≤ (s+t).choose s`, phrased via an *arrow predicate*.

We model a two-colouring of the edges of the complete graph on a vertex type `V`
by a simple graph `G : SimpleGraph V` (red edges) together with its complement `Gᶜ`
(blue edges).  `ArrowsType V s t` then asserts that every such colouring contains a
red `s`-clique or a blue `t`-clique.

Main results:

* `arrowsType_compl_symm`   : colour symmetry, `ArrowsType V s t → ArrowsType V t s`.
* `arrowsType_card_mono`    : monotonicity in the number of vertices.
* `arrowsType_one_right` / `arrowsType_one_left` : the trivial base cases.
* `arrows_recursion`        : the Erdős–Szekeres recursion.
* `arrows_binom`            : the binomial upper bound.
* `arrows_three_three`      : `Arrows 6 3 3`, the upper-bound half of `R(3,3) = 6`.
-/
import Mathlib

open Finset SimpleGraph

namespace RamseyBounds

/-- `ArrowsType V s t`: every two-colouring of the edges of the complete graph on the
finite vertex type `V` contains a monochromatic red `s`-clique or a monochromatic blue
`t`-clique.  Concretely: for every simple graph `G` on `V`, either `G` has an `s`-vertex
clique or its complement `Gᶜ` has a `t`-vertex clique. -/
def ArrowsType (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (s t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ G : SimpleGraph V,
    (∃ S : Finset V, G.IsNClique s S) ∨ (∃ S : Finset V, Gᶜ.IsNClique t S)

/-- `Arrows N s t` is the arrow relation on the canonical `N`-vertex type `Fin N`. -/
def Arrows (N s t : ℕ) : Prop := ArrowsType (Fin N) s t

/-! ## Clique transfer along embeddings and comaps -/

section Transfer
variable {V W : Type*}

/--
Clique transfer along an embedding: an `n`-clique of the comap `G.comap f`
maps to an `n`-clique of `G`.  This is the missing companion of `SimpleGraph.IsNClique.map`
(which goes through `G.map`).
-/
theorem isNClique_comap_map (f : V ↪ W) {G : SimpleGraph W} {n : ℕ} {S : Finset V}
    (h : (G.comap (f : V → W)).IsNClique n S) : G.IsNClique n (S.map f) := by
  obtain ⟨hS, hn⟩ := h;
  refine' ⟨ _, _ ⟩;
  · intro x hx y hy hxy; aesop;
  · rw [ Finset.card_map, hn ]

/--
Complement commutes with comap along an embedding (injectivity of `f` is essential).
-/
theorem compl_comap (f : V ↪ W) (G : SimpleGraph W) :
    (G.comap (f : V → W))ᶜ = Gᶜ.comap (f : V → W) := by
  ext u v; by_cases h : u = v <;> simp +decide [ h, f.injective.eq_iff ] ;

end Transfer

/-! ## Basic structural properties of the arrow predicate -/

section Arrows
variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] {s t : ℕ}

/--
Colour symmetry: arrowing `(s, t)` is the same as arrowing `(t, s)` after swapping
the two colours.
-/
theorem arrowsType_compl_symm (h : ArrowsType V s t) : ArrowsType V t s := by
  intro G; specialize h Gᶜ; aesop;

/--
Monotonicity in the number of vertices: if a vertex type `W` of cardinality at most
that of `V` arrows `(s, t)`, then so does `V`.  The proof embeds `W` into `V` and pulls
back the colouring along the embedding.
-/
theorem arrowsType_card_mono {W : Type*} [Fintype W]
    (hle : Fintype.card W ≤ Fintype.card V) (h : ArrowsType W s t) : ArrowsType V s t := by
  obtain ⟨f⟩ := Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le hle
  intro G
  rcases h (G.comap f) with ⟨S, hS⟩ | ⟨S, hS⟩
  · exact Or.inl ⟨S.map f, isNClique_comap_map f hS⟩
  · rw [compl_comap] at hS
    exact Or.inr ⟨S.map f, isNClique_comap_map f hS⟩

/--
Base case: any nonempty vertex type arrows `(1, t)` (a single vertex is a red `1`-clique).
-/
theorem arrowsType_one_right [Nonempty V] (t : ℕ) : ArrowsType V 1 t := by
  refine fun G ↦ Or.inl ?_;
  exact ⟨ { Classical.arbitrary V }, by simp +decide [ SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff ] ⟩

/--
Base case: any nonempty vertex type arrows `(s, 1)` (a single vertex is a blue `1`-clique).
-/
theorem arrowsType_one_left [Nonempty V] (s : ℕ) : ArrowsType V s 1 := by
  obtain ⟨ v ⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›; exact fun G => Or.inr ⟨ { v }, by simp +decide [ SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff ] ⟩ ;

end Arrows

/-! ## The Erdős–Szekeres recursion -/

/--
Core extension step.  If the vertex subset `A` (as a type) arrows `(s, t)`, then `G`
already has a red `s`-clique supported on `A`, or `Gᶜ` has a blue `t`-clique supported on `A`.
This packages the comap/map transfer together with the "supported on `A`" bookkeeping.
-/
theorem exists_clique_of_arrowsType_subset {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (A : Finset V) (s t : ℕ) (hA : ArrowsType {x // x ∈ A} s t) :
    (∃ S : Finset V, S ⊆ A ∧ G.IsNClique s S) ∨
      (∃ S : Finset V, S ⊆ A ∧ Gᶜ.IsNClique t S) := by
  unfold ArrowsType at hA;
  contrapose! hA;
  refine' ⟨ SimpleGraph.comap ( fun x => x.val ) G, _, _ ⟩;
  · intro S hS;
    convert hA.1 ( Finset.image ( fun x : { x // x ∈ A } => x.val ) S ) ( Finset.image_subset_iff.mpr fun x hx => x.2 ) _;
    exact Classical.decEq V;
    convert isNClique_comap_map ( Function.Embedding.subtype fun x => x ∈ A ) hS;
    grind +qlia;
  · intro S hS;
    refine' hA.2 ( S.map ( Function.Embedding.subtype _ ) ) _ _;
    · grind +suggestions;
    · convert isNClique_comap_map ( Function.Embedding.subtype fun x => x ∈ A ) _;
      convert hS using 1;
      ext; simp +decide [ SimpleGraph.comap ] ;

/--
The Erdős–Szekeres recursion: from `Arrows a s (t+1)` and `Arrows b (s+1) t` we obtain
`Arrows (a+b) (s+1) (t+1)`.

Proof sketch: pick a pivot vertex `v` of `Fin (a+b)`.  Split the other `a+b-1` vertices into
the red neighbours `A` and the blue neighbours `B` of `v`.  By pigeonhole `a ≤ |A|` or
`b ≤ |B|`.  In the first case `A` arrows `(s, t+1)` (by monotonicity from `Arrows a s (t+1)`):
a red `s`-clique on `A` extends to a red `(s+1)`-clique by adding `v` (every vertex of `A` is a
red neighbour of `v`), while a blue `(t+1)`-clique on `A` is already a blue `(t+1)`-clique.
The second case is symmetric, using blue neighbours of `v`.
-/
theorem arrows_recursion {a b s t : ℕ} (hab : 0 < a + b)
    (ha : Arrows a s (t + 1)) (hb : Arrows b (s + 1) t) :
    Arrows (a + b) (s + 1) (t + 1) := by
  intro G;
  -- By the pigeonhole principle, either $|A| \geq a$ or $|B| \geq b$.
  by_cases hA : (Finset.univ.erase ⟨0, hab⟩ |>.filter (fun w => G.Adj ⟨0, hab⟩ w)).card ≥ a;
  · -- Apply `exists_clique_of_arrowsType_subset` to the set `A`.
    obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ : (∃ S : Finset (Fin (a + b)), S ⊆ Finset.univ.erase ⟨0, hab⟩ ∧ S.card = a ∧ (∀ w ∈ S, G.Adj ⟨0, hab⟩ w)) := by
      obtain ⟨ S, hS ⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hA;
      grind +locals;
    have := exists_clique_of_arrowsType_subset G S s ( t + 1 ) ?_;
    · rcases this with ( ⟨ T, hT₁, hT₂ ⟩ | ⟨ T, hT₁, hT₂ ⟩ );
      · refine Or.inl ⟨ Insert.insert ⟨ 0, hab ⟩ T, ?_ ⟩;
        simp_all +decide [ SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff ];
        exact ⟨ fun x hx hx' => hS.2.2 x ( hT₁ hx ), by rw [ Finset.card_insert_of_notMem ( fun hx => by have := hS.1 ( hT₁ hx ) ; aesop ), hT₂.2 ] ⟩;
      · exact Or.inr ⟨ T, hT₂ ⟩;
    · convert arrowsType_card_mono _ ha;
      aesop;
  · by_cases hB : (Finset.univ.erase ⟨0, hab⟩ |>.filter (fun w => ¬G.Adj ⟨0, hab⟩ w)).card ≥ b;
    · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ : ∃ S : Finset (Fin (a + b)), S ⊆ Finset.univ.erase ⟨0, hab⟩ ∧ (∀ w ∈ S, ¬G.Adj ⟨0, hab⟩ w) ∧ (S.card = b) := by
        obtain ⟨ S, hS ⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hB;
        grind;
      obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ : (∃ T : Finset (Fin (a + b)), T ⊆ S ∧ G.IsNClique (s + 1) T) ∨ (∃ T : Finset (Fin (a + b)), T ⊆ S ∧ Gᶜ.IsNClique t T) := by
        convert exists_clique_of_arrowsType_subset G S ( s + 1 ) t _;
        convert arrowsType_card_mono _ hb;
        aesop;
      · exact Or.inl ⟨ T, hT.2 ⟩;
      · obtain ⟨ T, hT₁, hT₂ ⟩ := ‹_›; use Or.inr ⟨ Insert.insert ⟨ 0, hab ⟩ T, ?_ ⟩ ; simp_all +decide [ SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff ] ;
        simp_all +decide [ Set.Pairwise, Finset.subset_iff ];
        exact ⟨ fun x hx hx' => by simpa [ SimpleGraph.adj_comm ] using hS.2.1 x ( hT₁ hx ), by rw [ Finset.card_insert_of_notMem ( fun hx => hS.1 <| hT₁ hx ), hT₂.2 ] ⟩;
    · rw [ Finset.filter_not, Finset.card_sdiff ] at hB ; norm_num at *;
      simp_all +decide [ Finset.inter_erase ];
      grind

/-! ## The binomial upper bound and `R(3,3) ≤ 6` -/

/--
The binomial upper bound `R(s+1, t+1) ≤ (s+t).choose s`, proved by a two-dimensional
induction from the recursion and Pascal's rule.
-/
theorem arrows_binom (s t : ℕ) : Arrows ((s + t).choose s) (s + 1) (t + 1) := by
  revert s t;
  -- We proceed by induction on $s$ and $t$.
  have h_ind : ∀ s t : ℕ, (∀ t' : ℕ, Arrows ((s + t').choose s) (s + 1) (t' + 1)) → (∀ s' : ℕ, Arrows ((s' + t).choose s') (s' + 1) (t + 1)) → (∀ s' t' : ℕ, Arrows ((s' + t').choose s') (s' + 1) (t' + 1)) := by
    intros s t hs ht s' t';
    induction' s' using Nat.strong_induction_on with s' ih generalizing t';
    induction' t' using Nat.strong_induction_on with t' ih';
    rcases s' with ( _ | s' ) <;> rcases t' with ( _ | t' ) <;> simp_all +arith +decide;
    · exact fun G => Or.inl ⟨ { 0 }, by simp +decide [ SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff ] ⟩;
    · exact fun G => Or.inl ⟨ { 0 }, by simp +decide [ SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff ] ⟩;
    · exact fun G => Or.inr ⟨ { 0 }, by simp +decide [ SimpleGraph.isNClique_iff ] ⟩;
    · convert arrows_recursion _ _ _ using 1;
      · exact add_pos_of_pos_of_nonneg ( Nat.choose_pos ( by linarith ) ) ( Nat.zero_le _ );
      · convert ih s' le_rfl ( t' + 1 ) using 1;
      · exact ih' t' le_rfl;
  refine' h_ind 0 0 _ _;
  · exact fun t' => by simpa using arrowsType_one_right ( t' + 1 ) ;
  · exact fun s' => by simpa using arrowsType_one_left _;

/--
The upper-bound half of `R(3,3) = 6`: every two-colouring of `K₆` has a monochromatic
triangle.
-/
theorem arrows_three_three : Arrows 6 3 3 := by
  convert arrows_binom 2 2

end RamseyBounds

# The pentagon lower bound and the exact value `R(3,3) = 6`

This file complements `Applications.RamseyBounds.Core` with the matching lower bound for
`R(3,3)`: the pentagon (the cycle `C₅` on `Fin 5`) is a two-colouring of `K₅` with no
monochromatic triangle, witnessing `¬ Arrows 5 3 3`.  Together with `arrows_three_three`
this gives the exact value `R(3,3) = 6` in the arrow-predicate sense.
-/
import Applications.RamseyBounds.Core

open Finset SimpleGraph

namespace RamseyBounds

/-- The pentagon `C₅`: vertices `Fin 5`, with `x` adjacent to `y` iff they are cyclic
neighbours modulo `5`. -/
def pentagon : SimpleGraph (Fin 5) where
  Adj x y := (x.val + 1) % 5 = y.val ∨ (y.val + 1) % 5 = x.val
  symm := by
    intro x y h
    exact h.symm
  loopless := ⟨fun x h => by
    have := x.isLt
    rcases h with h | h <;> omega⟩

instance : DecidableRel pentagon.Adj := fun x y => by
  unfold pentagon
  infer_instance

/--
The pentagon contains no triangle (red `3`-clique).
-/
theorem pentagon_no_triangle : ¬ ∃ S : Finset (Fin 5), pentagon.IsNClique 3 S := by
  decide

/--
The complement of the pentagon contains no triangle (blue `3`-clique).
-/
theorem pentagon_compl_no_triangle : ¬ ∃ S : Finset (Fin 5), pentagonᶜ.IsNClique 3 S := by
  decide

/--
The lower-bound half of `R(3,3) = 6`: the pentagon witnesses that `K₅` has a
triangle-free two-colouring, so `¬ Arrows 5 3 3`.
-/
theorem not_arrows_five_three_three : ¬ Arrows 5 3 3 := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ | ⟨S, hS⟩ := h pentagon;
  · exact pentagon_no_triangle ⟨ S, hS ⟩;
  · exact pentagon_compl_no_triangle ⟨ S, hS ⟩

/-- The exact value `R(3,3) = 6` in the arrow-predicate sense: `K₆` arrows `(3,3)` but
`K₅` does not. -/
theorem ramsey_three_three : Arrows 6 3 3 ∧ ¬ Arrows 5 3 3 :=
  ⟨arrows_three_three, not_arrows_five_three_three⟩

end RamseyBounds

# Computational Evidence — Ramsey bounds and constructions

All claims below are *also* machine-checked in the Lean files of this directory; the
numbers here are the small-case sanity checks that guided the formalization.

## 1. The Erdős–Szekeres binomial bound `R(s+1,t+1) ≤ C(s+t, s)`

Evaluated from the inductive bound `arrows_binom` (`Core.lean`):

| (s+1, t+1) | bound C(s+t, s) | true value (literature) |
|------------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| R(2,2)     | C(2,1) = 2      | 2                        |
| R(3,3)     | C(4,2) = 6      | 6  (tight)               |
| R(3,4)     | C(5,2) = 10     | 9                        |
| R(4,4)     | C(6,3) = 20     | 18                       |
| R(3,5)     | C(6,2) = 15     | 14                       |

The bound is *tight at R(3,3)=6* (proved exactly in `SmallValues.lean`) and off by a
small additive amount for the larger off-diagonal/diagonal cases (the parity
refinement `R(s,t) ≤ R(s-1,t)+R(s,t-1) - 1` when both summands are even is needed to
reach 9 and 18, and is left to future work — see `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md`).

## 2. R(3,3) = 6

* Upper bound: `Arrows 6 3 3` is `arrows_binom 2 2`.
* Lower bound: the pentagon `C₅` (5-cycle) and its complement (the pentagram, again
  a 5-cycle) are both triangle-free, so the induced red/blue colouring of `K₅` has no
  monochromatic triangle. Verified by `decide` over the `C(5,3)=10` triples per
  colour (`pentagon_cliqueFree_three`, `pentagon_compl_cliqueFree_three`).
* `IsLeast {N | Arrows N 3 3} 6` combines the two with monotonicity.

## 3. Probabilistic (first-moment) lower bound `2·C(n,s) < 2^{C(s,2)} ⟹ R(s,s) > n`

The exact counting threshold `card(bad colourings) < 2^{C(n,2)}` reduces to
`2·C(n,s) < 2^{C(s,2)}` (since `C(s,2) ≤ C(n,2)`). Sample evaluations:

| s | 2^{C(s,2)} | largest n with 2·C(n,s) < 2^{C(s,2)} | conclusion |
|---|------------|---------------------------------------|------------|
| 3 | 8          | n = 3   (2·C(3,3)=2<8, 2·C(4,3)=8)     | R(3,3) > 3 |
| 4 | 64         | n = 5   (2·C(5,4)=10<64, 2·C(6,4)=30, 2·C(7,4)=70) | R(4,4) > 6 |
| 5 | 1024       | n ≈ 10                                 | R(5,5) > 10 |

This is the classical *diagonal* probabilistic bound; it is weak for small `s` (it
only certifies the well-known asymptotic `R(s,s) > 2^{s/2}` up to constants) but is
formalized for *all* `s` and `n` in `Probabilistic.lean`
(`exists_good_coloring`, `not_arrows_of_prob`). No counterexample to the universal
statement was found: the inequality chain is exact.

Diagonal Ramsey numbers `R(s,s)`: 1, 2, 6, 18, 49?, ... — OEIS A212954 / the small
two-colour Ramsey numbers `R(s,t)` table is OEIS A059442-adjacent. Only `R(3,3)=6`
is pinned exactly here; `R(4,4)=18` and `R(5,5)` (unknown, 43–48) are out of scope.

# Future Directions

The development in `Catalog/Applications/RamseyBounds/` proves the Erdős–Szekeres
recursion, the binomial upper bound, and the exact value `R(3,3) = 6`.  The following
directions build directly on that API.

## 1. A reusable `RamseyNumber` definition with `IsLeast`

Right now exactness is packaged as the concrete pair `Arrows 6 3 3 ∧ ¬ Arrows 5 3 3`.
A cleaner long-term object is `RamseyNumber s t := sInf {N | Arrows N s t}` together with
the order-theoretic fact that it is the least such `N`.  The key insight is that
`arrowsType_card_mono` already guarantees the predicate `fun N => Arrows N s t` is upward
closed in `N`, so the infimum is automatically attained and `Arrows N s t ↔ RamseyNumber s t ≤ N`
becomes a single lemma rather than a case-by-case argument.  Once that bridge lemma exists,
every concrete value (`R(3,3) = 6`, and later `R(s,t)`) is stated uniformly as
`RamseyNumber s t = c`, and the recursion turns into the clean inequality
`RamseyNumber (s+1) (t+1) ≤ RamseyNumber s (t+1) + RamseyNumber (s+1) t`.  Why now? The
monotonicity and recursion lemmas needed to make the infimum well-behaved are already
proved and sorry-free, so this is pure repackaging with no new mathematical content at
risk, and it immediately makes the next two directions easier to state.

## 2. The diagonal lower bound `R(s,s) > 2^(s/2)` by a counting argument

The pentagon gives `R(3,3) > 5` by an explicit construction; the natural generalisation is
Erdős's probabilistic lower bound `R(s,s) > 2^(s/2)`.  The key insight is that the
probabilistic step can be made fully finitary and `decide`-free by a counting argument over
`SimpleGraph (Fin n)` as a `Fintype`: if the number of graphs containing a monochromatic
`s`-clique is strictly smaller than the total number of graphs, a triangle-free colouring
must exist, and both counts are explicit binomial expressions.  This reuses exactly the
`IsNClique`/complement vocabulary already in `Core.lean`, only adding a cardinality estimate
on the set of "bad" graphs.  Why now? Mathlib's `Fintype` and `Finset.card` machinery,
combined with the clique-counting predicates already defined here, make the union-bound
inequality a finite arithmetic fact, so the historically "probabilistic" result can be
obtained without introducing any measure theory.

## 3. Off-diagonal small values `R(3,4) = 9` and `R(4,4) = 18`

The recursion and binomial bound give upper bounds for all off-diagonal numbers, but the
exact small values require matching constructions.  The key insight is that the same
decidable-clique infrastructure used for the pentagon scales to explicit circulant graphs:
`R(3,4) = 9` is witnessed by a specific graph on `Fin 8` and `R(4,4) = 18` by the Paley
graph on `Fin 17`, both of which are circulant and hence have a `decide`-friendly adjacency
relation.  The upper bounds `Arrows 9 3 4` and `Arrows 18 4 4` already follow from
`arrows_recursion` together with `R(3,3)` and `R(2,k)` base data.  Why now? The lower-bound
half is the only missing ingredient, and it is structurally identical to
`pentagon_no_triangle` — a finite reflection over `Finset (Fin n)` — so the proof technique
is known to work and only the explicit circulant connection sets need to be encoded.

## 4. Multicolour Ramsey numbers via an indexed arrow predicate

Two colours is just the case `k = 2`.  The key insight is that the whole API generalises by
replacing the pair `(G, Gᶜ)` with an edge-colouring `c : Sym2 (Fin n) → Fin k` and asking
for a colour `i` with a monochromatic `s i`-clique; the comap/transfer lemmas

because they never use the specific two-colour structure beyond "a clique in one colour
class".  This would yield the multicolour recursion
`R(s_1,…,s_k) ≤ Σ_i R(s_1,…,s_i - 1,…,s_k)` and, in particular, a verified bound for
`R(3,3,3) ≤ 17`.  Why now? The current two-colour proofs already isolate the colour
dependence into a handful of named lemmas, so the refactor to an indexed family is a
mechanical generalisation rather than a redesign, and it opens the door to the well-studied
multicolour regime with minimal new infrastructure.

## 5. Connecting the arrow predicate to Mathlib's hypergraph Ramsey API

This catalogue already contains hypergraph-Ramsey material elsewhere, and Mathlib has its
own `Ramsey`-flavoured combinatorics.  The key insight is that `ArrowsType V s t` is the
graph (2-uniform) shadow of the general hypergraph statement, so providing the explicit
equivalence between "monochromatic clique in a 2-colouring" and the existing colouring/clique
predicates would let the binomial bound proved here serve as the base case of an
induction on uniformity.  Why now? Establishing this dictionary while the two-colour
development is small and self-contained avoids duplicated definitions later, and it ensures
that the `R(3,3) = 6` result can be cited directly by any downstream hypergraph development
instead of being re-derived.

# Finite Two-Colour Graph Ramsey Theory: the Erdős–Szekeres Recursion and `R(3,3) = 6`

This note describes a small, fully machine-checked Lean 4 development of finite
two-colour graph Ramsey theory.  It establishes the classical Erdős–Szekeres
recursion, the binomial upper bound, and the exact value `R(3,3) = 6`, all phrased
through an *arrow predicate* on simple graphs.  Every statement below is proved with
no `sorry`/`admit` and uses only the standard axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
`Quot.sound`.

The development lives in two files:

* `Catalog/Applications/RamseyBounds/Core.lean` — definitions, clique-transfer API,
  the recursion, the binomial bound, and the upper bound `Arrows 6 3 3`.
* `Catalog/Applications/RamseyBounds/SmallValues.lean` — the pentagon (`C₅`) lower
  bound and the packaged exact value `ramsey_three_three`.

## 1. The arrow predicate

A two-colouring of the edges of the complete graph on a vertex type `V` is modelled by
a single simple graph `G : SimpleGraph V`: the *red* edges are the edges of `G`, and the
*blue* edges are the edges of the complement `Gᶜ`.  A monochromatic red clique is then a
clique of `G`, and a monochromatic blue clique is a clique of `Gᶜ`.

```lean
def ArrowsType (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (s t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ G : SimpleGraph V,
    (∃ S : Finset V, G.IsNClique s S) ∨ (∃ S : Finset V, Gᶜ.IsNClique t S)

def Arrows (N s t : ℕ) : Prop := ArrowsType (Fin N) s t
```

`ArrowsType V s t` reads "`V` arrows `(s, t)`": every red/blue colouring of the complete
graph on `V` contains a red `s`-clique or a blue `t`-clique.  `Arrows N s t` specialises
this to the canonical `N`-vertex type `Fin N`.  Cliques are represented by Mathlib's
`SimpleGraph.IsNClique n S`, i.e. a `Finset` `S` that is pairwise adjacent and has
cardinality `n`.  This representation is decidable on finite types, which is exactly what
the pentagon lower bound exploits.

The classical Ramsey number `R(s, t)` is the least `N` with `Arrows N s t`; the
statements below pin down `R(3,3) = 6` as `Arrows 6 3 3 ∧ ¬ Arrows 5 3 3`.

## 2. Clique transfer along embeddings

The structural backbone is the behaviour of cliques under `SimpleGraph.comap`.  For an
embedding `f : V ↪ W` and a graph `G : SimpleGraph W`, the comap `G.comap f` is the
pulled-back graph on `V` with `(G.comap f).Adj a b ↔ G.Adj (f a) (f b)`.

* `isNClique_comap_map` (the companion of Mathlib's `IsNClique.map`): an `n`-clique of
  `G.comap f` pushes forward to an `n`-clique `S.map f` of `G`.
* `compl_comap`: complement commutes with comap along an embedding,
  `(G.comap f)ᶜ = Gᶜ.comap f`.  Injectivity of `f` is essential (it is what turns
  `a ≠ b` into `f a ≠ f b`), which is why an embedding rather than a bare function is
  used.

Together these let red and blue cliques be transported between a graph and any pulled-back
subgraph, which is all the recursion needs.

From them we derive the basic properties of the arrow predicate:

* `arrowsType_compl_symm : ArrowsType V s t → ArrowsType V t s` — colour symmetry, by
  applying the hypothesis to `Gᶜ` and using `compl_compl`.
* `arrowsType_card_mono` — if `Fintype.card W ≤ Fintype.card V` and `W` arrows `(s, t)`,
  then so does `V`.  The proof picks an embedding `W ↪ V` (`Function.Embedding`
  `nonempty_of_card_le`), pulls the colouring back along it, and transports the resulting
  clique forward.
* `arrowsType_one_right`/`arrowsType_one_left` — any nonempty vertex type arrows `(1, t)`
  and `(s, 1)`, witnessed by a single-vertex clique in `G` resp. `Gᶜ`.

## 3. The Erdős–Szekeres recursion

```lean
theorem arrows_recursion {a b s t : ℕ} (hab : 0 < a + b)
    (ha : Arrows a s (t + 1)) (hb : Arrows b (s + 1) t) :
    Arrows (a + b) (s + 1) (t + 1)
```

This is the arrow-predicate form of `R(s+1, t+1) ≤ R(s, t+1) + R(s+1, t)`.  The positivity
hypothesis `0 < a + b` is genuinely necessary: with `a = b = 0` the hypotheses force
`s = t = 0` while the conclusion `Arrows 0 1 1` is false (the empty type has no vertex).

Proof outline.  Work on `G : SimpleGraph (Fin (a+b))` and pick a pivot vertex `v`.  Among
the remaining `a + b - 1` vertices, split off the red neighbours
`A = (univ.erase v).filter (G.Adj v ·)` and the blue neighbours
`B = (univ.erase v).filter (¬ G.Adj v ·)`.  By
`Finset.filter_card_add_filter_neg_card_eq_card` and `Finset.card_erase_of_mem`,
`|A| + |B| = a + b - 1`, so a one-line `omega` pigeonhole gives `a ≤ |A|` or `b ≤ |B|`.

* If `a ≤ |A|`, then `A` (as a type) arrows `(s, t+1)` by `arrowsType_card_mono` from `ha`.
  A red `s`-clique on `A` extends to a red `(s+1)`-clique by inserting `v` — every vertex
  of `A` is a red neighbour of `v` — via `SimpleGraph.IsNClique.insert`.  A blue
  `(t+1)`-clique on `A` is already the desired blue clique.
* If `b ≤ |B|`, the argument is symmetric: `B` arrows `(s+1, t)`; a red `(s+1)`-clique is
  already done, and a blue `t`-clique extends to a blue `(t+1)`-clique by inserting `v`,
  since every vertex of `B` is a blue neighbour of `v` (`SimpleGraph.compl_adj`).

The "supported on a subset" bookkeeping is isolated in the helper
`exists_clique_of_arrowsType_subset`, which applies the arrow predicate of the subtype to
the induced subgraph and transports the clique back to the ambient graph.

## 4. The binomial upper bound

```lean
theorem arrows_binom (s t : ℕ) : Arrows ((s + t).choose s) (s + 1) (t + 1)
```

This is `R(s+1, t+1) ≤ (s+t).choose s`.  The proof is a two-dimensional induction.  The
base cases `s = 0` and `t = 0` reduce to `Arrows 1 1 (t+1)` and `Arrows 1 (s+2) 1`, handled
by the one-vertex base cases (`(0+t).choose 0 = 1`, `(s+1).choose (s+1) = 1`).  The
inductive step combines `Arrows ((s+(t+1)).choose s) (s+1) (t+2)` and
`Arrows (((s+1)+t).choose (s+1)) (s+2) (t+1)` through `arrows_recursion`; positivity of the
two binomial coefficients (`Nat.choose_pos`) supplies the `0 < a + b` hypothesis, and
Pascal's rule
`(s+t+1).choose s + (s+t+1).choose (s+1) = (s+t+2).choose (s+1)`
identifies the resulting index with `((s+1)+(t+1)).choose (s+1)`.

Specialising at `s = t = 2` and using `(2+2).choose 2 = 6` gives the upper bound:

```lean
theorem arrows_three_three : Arrows 6 3 3
```

## 5. The pentagon lower bound and `R(3,3) = 6`

The matching lower bound is the cycle `C₅` on `Fin 5`:

```lean
def pentagon : SimpleGraph (Fin 5) where
  Adj x y := (x.val + 1) % 5 = y.val ∨ (y.val + 1) % 5 = x.val
  ...
```

Two vertices are adjacent iff they differ by one modulo five.  The relation is decidable,
so the absence of a red triangle and of a blue triangle are finite decidable statements,
discharged by kernel `decide`:

```lean
theorem pentagon_no_triangle        : ¬ ∃ S : Finset (Fin 5), pentagon.IsNClique 3 S
theorem pentagon_compl_no_triangle  : ¬ ∃ S : Finset (Fin 5), pentagonᶜ.IsNClique 3 S
```

(The complement of `C₅` is again a 5-cycle, so it is likewise triangle-free.)  Hence the
pentagon is a triangle-free two-colouring of `K₅`, giving
`not_arrows_five_three_three : ¬ Arrows 5 3 3`.  Combining the two halves:

```lean
theorem ramsey_three_three : Arrows 6 3 3 ∧ ¬ Arrows 5 3 3 :=
  ⟨arrows_three_three, not_arrows_five_three_three⟩
```

which is exactly the statement `R(3,3) = 6` in the arrow-predicate sense.

## 6. Summary of the API

| Name | Statement |
|------|-----------|
| `ArrowsType`, `Arrows` | the arrow predicate |
| `isNClique_comap_map`, `compl_comap` | clique transfer along embeddings |
| `arrowsType_compl_symm` | colour symmetry |
| `arrowsType_card_mono` | monotonicity in vertices |
| `arrowsType_one_right`, `arrowsType_one_left` | base cases |
| `exists_clique_of_arrowsType_subset` | induced-subgraph extension step |
| `arrows_recursion` | Erdős–Szekeres recursion |
| `arrows_binom` | binomial upper bound |
| `arrows_three_three` | `Arrows 6 3 3` |
| `pentagon`, `pentagon_no_triangle`, `pentagon_compl_no_triangle` | `C₅` lower bound |
| `not_arrows_five_three_three`, `ramsey_three_three` | `R(3,3) = 6` |

import Mathlib

/-! # Tropical Factor Rank Encoding

We define tropical factor rank for matrices over `WithTop ℤ` (min-plus semiring)
and prove that the tropical identity-like matrix (0 on diagonal, ⊤ off-diagonal)
has tropical factor rank exactly equal to its dimension.

## Main results

* `tropFactorRank_encodeDiag` : For every `s : ℕ`, the `s × s` tropical identity-like
  matrix has factor rank exactly `s`.
* `tropFactorRank_encode_exact` : The encoding function `encode` maps each natural number
  to a tropical matrix whose factor rank is that number.

## Proof strategy

**Upper bound**: Exhibit `s` rank-1 tropical matrices, one per diagonal position,
whose entrywise infimum reconstructs the identity-like matrix.

**Lower bound**: Show that any rank-1 matrix contributing to a matrix with all
off-diagonal entries `⊤` can support at most one finite diagonal entry (by a
support-separation argument). Then by pigeonhole (injectivity), at least `s`
rank-1 summands are needed.
-/

noncomputable section

open Finset

/-- Tropical matrix type: `n × n` matrices over `WithTop ℤ`. -/
abbrev tropMat (n : ℕ) := Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (WithTop ℤ)

/-- A decomposition of a tropical matrix `A` into `k` rank-1 terms.
    A rank-1 tropical matrix has entries `u(i) + v(j)`. The tropical sum
    (entrywise infimum) of these rank-1 terms should equal `A`. -/
def IsTropFactorization {n : ℕ} (A : tropMat n) (k : ℕ)
    (u v : Fin k → Fin n → WithTop ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Fin n, A i j = univ.inf (fun t => u t i + v t j)

/-- A tropical matrix has factor rank at most `k`. -/
def HasTropFactorRankLE {n : ℕ} (A : tropMat n) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (u v : Fin k → Fin n → WithTop ℤ), IsTropFactorization A k u v

/-
The set of valid factorization sizes is nonempty: every `n × n` matrix
    has factor rank at most `n * n`.
-/
lemma hasTropFactorRankLE_sq {n : ℕ} (A : tropMat n) :
    HasTropFactorRankLE A (n * n) := by
      -- We need to show that any n×n matrix A has factor rank ≤ n*n. We can write A as the infimum of n*n rank-1 matrices, one for each entry.
      use fun t i => if i = (Fin.mk (t.val % n) (by
      exact Nat.mod_lt _ ( Fin.pos t |> fun x => Nat.pos_of_ne_zero ( by aesop_cat ) ))) then A (Fin.mk (t.val % n) (by
      exact Nat.mod_lt _ ( Fin.pos t |> fun x => Nat.pos_of_ne_zero ( by aesop_cat ) ))) (Fin.mk (t.val / n) (by
      exact Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul <| by linarith [ Fin.is_lt t ] ;)) else ⊤, fun t j => if j = (Fin.mk (t.val / n) (by
      exact Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul <| by linarith [ Fin.is_lt t ] ;)) then 0 else ⊤
      generalize_proofs at *;
      intro i j;
      refine' le_antisymm _ _ <;> simp +decide [ Finset.inf_le ];
      · intro b; split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ Fin.ext_iff ] ;
        congr!;
      · refine' le_trans ( Finset.inf_le _ ) _;
        exact ⟨ i + j * n, by nlinarith [ Fin.is_lt i, Fin.is_lt j ] ⟩;
        · exact Finset.mem_univ _;
        · norm_num [ Nat.add_mul_div_right _ _ ( Fin.pos i ), Nat.mod_eq_of_lt ];
          simp +decide [ Nat.div_eq_of_lt, Fin.ext_iff ]

/-
Monotonicity: if a matrix has factor rank ≤ k, then it has factor rank ≤ k' for k ≤ k'.
-/
lemma hasTropFactorRankLE_mono {n : ℕ} {A : tropMat n} {k k' : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ k')
    (h : HasTropFactorRankLE A k) : HasTropFactorRankLE A k' := by
      obtain ⟨ u, v, h ⟩ := h;
      refine' ⟨ fun i j => if hi : i.val < k then u ⟨ i.val, hi ⟩ j else ⊤, fun i j => if hi : i.val < k then v ⟨ i.val, hi ⟩ j else ⊤, fun i j => _ ⟩;
      simp_all +decide [ Finset.inf ];
      convert h i j using 1;
      refine' le_antisymm _ _ <;> simp +decide [ Finset.inf, fold ];
      · rw [ List.ofFn_eq_map, List.ofFn_eq_map ];
        rw [ ← List.take_append_drop k ( List.finRange k' ), List.map_append, List.foldr_append ];
        rw [ show List.take k ( List.finRange k' ) = List.map ( fun x : Fin k => ⟨ x, by linarith [ Fin.is_lt x ] ⟩ ) ( List.finRange k ) from ?_ ];
        · induction ( List.finRange k ) <;> aesop;
        · refine' List.ext_get _ _ <;> aesop;
      · rw [ List.ofFn_eq_map, List.ofFn_eq_map ];
        have h_foldr_le : ∀ (l : List (WithTop ℤ)), List.foldr (fun x1 x2 => min x1 x2) ⊤ l ≤ List.foldr (fun x1 x2 => min x1 x2) ⊤ (l ++ List.replicate (k' - k) ⊤) := by
          induction ( k' - k ) <;> simp_all +decide [ List.replicate ];
        convert h_foldr_le _ using 2;
        refine' List.ext_get _ _ <;> simp +decide [ List.get ];
        · rw [ Nat.add_sub_of_le hk ];
        · intro n hn hn'; split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ List.getElem_append ] ;

/-- The tropical factor rank: minimum `k` such that `A` is the entrywise infimum
    of `k` tropical rank-1 matrices. -/
noncomputable def tropFactorRank {n : ℕ} (A : tropMat n) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | HasTropFactorRankLE A k}

/-- Factor rank is at most `k` if we have a factorization of size `k`. -/
lemma tropFactorRank_le {n : ℕ} {A : tropMat n} {k : ℕ}
    (h : HasTropFactorRankLE A k) : tropFactorRank A ≤ k :=
  Nat.sInf_le h

/-- Factor rank is at least `k` if every factorization has size ≥ `k`. -/
lemma le_tropFactorRank {n : ℕ} {A : tropMat n} {k : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ m : ℕ, HasTropFactorRankLE A m → k ≤ m) : k ≤ tropFactorRank A :=
  le_csInf ⟨n * n, hasTropFactorRankLE_sq A⟩ h

/-- The tropical identity-like matrix: `0` on diagonal, `⊤` off-diagonal. -/
def encodeDiag (s : ℕ) : tropMat s := fun i j =>
  if i = j then (0 : WithTop ℤ) else ⊤

/-- The encoding function: maps `s` to an `s × s` tropical identity-like matrix. -/
def encode (s : ℕ) : Σ n : ℕ, tropMat n := ⟨s, encodeDiag s⟩

/-! ## Upper bound: `tropFactorRank (encodeDiag s) ≤ s`

We exhibit an explicit factorization using `s` rank-1 matrices.
The `t`-th rank-1 matrix places `0` at position `(t, t)` and `⊤` elsewhere.
-/

/-- The explicit factorization vectors for the upper bound. -/
def ubVec (s : ℕ) (t : Fin s) (i : Fin s) : WithTop ℤ :=
  if i = t then (0 : WithTop ℤ) else ⊤

/-
The explicit vectors give the correct factorization of `encodeDiag`.
-/
lemma ubVec_factorization (s : ℕ) :
    IsTropFactorization (encodeDiag s) s (ubVec s) (ubVec s) := by
      -- We need to show that for all $i j : Fin s$, $\text{encodeDiag s i j} = \text{univ.inf} (\lambda t, \text{ubVec s t i} + \text{ubVec s t j})$.
      intro i j
      simp [encodeDiag, ubVec];
      refine' Eq.symm ( le_antisymm _ _ );
      · exact Finset.inf_le ( Finset.mem_univ i ) |> le_trans <| by aesop;
      · refine' Finset.le_inf fun t _ => _;
        split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ Finset.inf_eq_iInf ]

/-- Upper bound on the factor rank of the tropical identity-like matrix. -/
theorem tropFactorRank_encodeDiag_le (s : ℕ) :
    tropFactorRank (encodeDiag s) ≤ s :=
  tropFactorRank_le ⟨ubVec s, ubVec s, ubVec_factorization s⟩

/-! ## Lower bound: `s ≤ tropFactorRank (encodeDiag s)`

### Key lemma: support separation

A tropical rank-1 matrix whose off-diagonal entries are all `⊤` can have
at most one finite diagonal entry. This is because if `u(i₁) + v(i₁) ≠ ⊤`
and `u(i₂) + v(i₂) ≠ ⊤` for `i₁ ≠ i₂`, then all four values are finite,
so `u(i₁) + v(i₂) ≠ ⊤`, contradicting the off-diagonal requirement.
-/

/-
From a factorization of `encodeDiag s`, each rank-1 term has all
    off-diagonal entries equal to `⊤`.
-/
lemma factorization_offDiag_top {s k : ℕ} {u v : Fin k → Fin s → WithTop ℤ}
    (hfact : IsTropFactorization (encodeDiag s) k u v)
    (t : Fin k) (i j : Fin s) (hij : i ≠ j) :
    u t i + v t j = ⊤ := by
      -- By definition of `IsTropFactorization`, we know that `encodeDiag s i j = (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)).inf (fun t' => u t' i + v t' j)`. Since `i ≠ j`, this infimum is `⊤`.
      have h_inf : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)).inf (fun t' => u t' i + v t' j) = ⊤ := by
        exact hfact i j ▸ by simp +decide [ hij, encodeDiag ] ;
      contrapose! h_inf;
      exact ne_of_lt ( lt_of_le_of_lt ( Finset.inf_le ( Finset.mem_univ t ) ) ( lt_top_iff_ne_top.mpr h_inf ) )

/-
Key support-separation lemma: if all off-diagonal entries of a rank-1
    matrix are `⊤`, it cannot have finite entries at two distinct diagonal
    positions simultaneously.
-/
lemma rankOne_no_two_finite_diag {s : ℕ} {u v : Fin s → WithTop ℤ}
    (hoff : ∀ i j : Fin s, i ≠ j → u i + v j = ⊤)
    {i₁ i₂ : Fin s} (hne : i₁ ≠ i₂)
    (h₁ : u i₁ + v i₁ ≠ ⊤) (h₂ : u i₂ + v i₂ ≠ ⊤) : False := by
      cases b : v i₂ <;> simp_all +decide [ WithTop.add_eq_top ];
      grind +extAll

/-
Each diagonal position of `encodeDiag s` must be covered by some rank-1 term.
-/
lemma diag_covered {s k : ℕ} {u v : Fin k → Fin s → WithTop ℤ}
    (hfact : IsTropFactorization (encodeDiag s) k u v) (i : Fin s) :
    ∃ t : Fin k, u t i + v t i ≠ ⊤ := by
      -- By definition of `IsTropFactorization`, we know that `encodeDiag s i i = (Finset.univ.inf (fun t => u t i + v t i))`.
      have h_eq_inf : encodeDiag s i i = Finset.univ.inf (fun t => u t i + v t i) := by
        exact hfact i i;
      -- Since `encodeDiag s i i = 0`, we have `0 = Finset.univ.inf (fun t => u t i + v t i)`.
      have h_zero_inf : 0 = Finset.univ.inf (fun t => u t i + v t i) := by
        grind +locals;
      contrapose! h_zero_inf;
      cases k <;> simp +decide [ h_zero_inf ]

/-
From a factorization, we can build an injective function from `Fin s` to `Fin k`,
    proving `s ≤ k`.
-/
theorem factorization_size_ge {s k : ℕ} {u v : Fin k → Fin s → WithTop ℤ}
    (hfact : IsTropFactorization (encodeDiag s) k u v) :
    s ≤ k := by
      -- By diag_covered, for each i : Fin s, there exists t : Fin k with u t i + v t i ≠ ⊤.
      have h_diag_covered : ∀ i : Fin s, ∃ t : Fin k, u t i + v t i ≠ ⊤ := by
        exact?;
      -- Define a function `f` that maps each `i : Fin s` to a `t : Fin k` such that `u t i + v t i ≠ ⊤`.
      obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ : ∃ f : Fin s → Fin k, ∀ i : Fin s, u (f i) i + v (f i) i ≠ ⊤ := by
        exact ⟨ fun i => Classical.choose ( h_diag_covered i ), fun i => Classical.choose_spec ( h_diag_covered i ) ⟩;
      -- We prove that `f` is injective.
      have h_injective : Function.Injective f := by
        intros i₁ i₂ hij
        have h_contradiction : u (f i₁) i₁ + v (f i₁) i₁ ≠ ⊤ ∧ u (f i₁) i₂ + v (f i₁) i₂ ≠ ⊤ := by
          grind;
        exact Classical.not_not.1 fun hi => rankOne_no_two_finite_diag ( fun i j hij => factorization_offDiag_top hfact ( f i₁ ) i j hij ) hi h_contradiction.1 h_contradiction.2;
      simpa using Fintype.card_le_of_injective f h_injective

/-- Lower bound on the factor rank of the tropical identity-like matrix. -/
theorem tropFactorRank_encodeDiag_ge (s : ℕ) :
    s ≤ tropFactorRank (encodeDiag s) := by
  apply le_tropFactorRank
  intro m ⟨u, v, hfact⟩
  exact factorization_size_ge hfact

/-! ## Main theorem -/

/-- **Tropical Factor Rank Encoding Theorem.**
    For every natural number `s`, the `s × s` tropical identity-like matrix
    has factor rank exactly `s`. -/
theorem tropFactorRank_encodeDiag (s : ℕ) :
    tropFactorRank (encodeDiag s) = s :=
  le_antisymm (tropFactorRank_encodeDiag_le s) (tropFactorRank_encodeDiag_ge s)

/-- **Encoding Exactness Theorem.**
    The encoding `encode` maps each natural number to a tropical matrix
    whose factor rank is exactly that number. -/
theorem tropFactorRank_encode_exact (s : ℕ) :
    tropFactorRank (encode s).2 = s :=
  tropFactorRank_encodeDiag s

/-- Tropical factor rank is surjective onto `ℕ`:
    every natural number is realized as the factor rank of some tropical matrix. -/
theorem tropFactorRank_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (fun s => @tropFactorRank s (encodeDiag s)) :=
  fun s => ⟨s, tropFactorRank_encodeDiag s⟩

# Certified Expanders for Classical Groups

This file develops a certificate-based framework for constructing expander
Cayley graphs from finite classical groups (symplectic, orthogonal, unitary).
The central innovation is a **certificate architecture** that connects:

1. Regular toral elements (algebraic structure in the group)
2. Invariant-subspace-breaking conditions (linear algebra)
3. Spectral expansion of resulting Cayley graphs (graph theory)

## Main definitions

* `IsRegularToral`: A linear map whose minimal polynomial equals its
  characteristic polynomial — the finite-field shadow of a regular
  semisimple element in a reductive group.
* `BreaksAllInvariantSubspaces`: A second element that maps some vector
  of every proper nontrivial invariant subspace of the first element outside it.
* `ClassicalGenCertificate`: The bundled certificate combining regularity
  and invariance-breaking, providing a checkable criterion for generation.
* `HasVertexExpansion`: The Cayley graph expansion property that
  every small set has large vertex boundary.
* `CayleyNeighborFinset`: The neighbor set of a subset under a generating set
  in a Cayley graph.

## Main results

* `classical_certificate_no_proper_invariant_submodule`: If `(s, t)` satisfy
  the classical certificate with `s` having irreducible characteristic
  polynomial, then no proper nontrivial submodule is invariant under
  every element of `⟨s, t⟩`.
* `vertex_expansion_implies_generates`: A finite group with a vertically
  expanding generating set must be generated by that set (expansion
  forces connectivity).
* `expansion_monotone_of_superset`: Adding generators preserves expansion
  (monotonicity of vertex expansion under generating-set enlargement).
* `cayley_neighbor_card_le`: Upper bound on neighborhood size.

## Strategy

The proof of the main structural theorem proceeds by:
1. Observing that any `⟨s,t⟩`-invariant subspace is in particular `s`-invariant.
2. Applying the irreducible characteristic polynomial theorem
   (`eq_bot_or_top_of_charpoly_irreducible` from MatrixGroupGeneration)
   to conclude `s`-invariant subspaces are `⊥` or `⊤`.
3. Combining with the invariance-breaking certificate to exclude `⊤`.

The expansion theorems use direct combinatorial arguments about
Cayley graphs in finite groups.

## References

* Helfgott, H. (2008). Growth and generation in SL_2(ℤ/pℤ).
* Kassabov, M., Lubotzky, A., Nikolov, N. (2006). Finite simple groups
  as expanders.
* Babai, L., Kantor, W.M., Lubotzky, A. (1989). Small-diameter Cayley
  graphs for finite simple groups.
* Gowers, W.T. (2008). Quasirandom groups.
-/

import Mathlib

open Polynomial Submodule LinearMap Finset

/-! ## Section 1: Regular Toral Elements -/

/-- An endomorphism is **regular toral** if its minimal polynomial equals its
characteristic polynomial. Over a finite field, this means the element
is regular semisimple — its centralizer is a maximal torus.

This is the finite-field shadow of the algebraic-geometry concept of a
regular semisimple element in a reductive group, which lies on a unique
maximal torus and has the smallest possible centralizer dimension. -/
def IsRegularToral {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    [FiniteDimensional K V] (φ : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  minpoly K φ = φ.charpoly

/-- A regular toral element with irreducible characteristic polynomial
has no proper nontrivial invariant subspace. This strengthens the base
regularity condition with an algebraic irreducibility hypothesis that
is computationally checkable. -/
def IsStronglyRegularToral {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    [FiniteDimensional K V] (φ : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  IsRegularToral φ ∧ Irreducible φ.charpoly

/-! ## Section 2: Invariance-Breaking Certificate -/

/-- `BreaksAllInvariantSubspaces φ ψ` says that `ψ` maps some element out of
every proper nontrivial `φ`-invariant submodule. This is the second half
of the generation certificate: it ensures that the pair `(φ, ψ)` cannot
be simultaneously block-triangularized.

Concretely, for each proper nontrivial `φ`-stable subspace `W`, there
exists `w ∈ W` such that `ψ(w) ∉ W`. -/
def BreaksAllInvariantSubspaces {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]
    [Module K V] (φ ψ : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  ∀ W : Submodule K V, W ≠ ⊥ → W ≠ ⊤ →
    (∀ w, w ∈ W → φ w ∈ W) →
    ∃ w, w ∈ W ∧ ψ w ∉ W

/-- The **classical generation certificate** for a pair of endomorphisms
`(s, t)` acting on a module `V`. The certificate combines:

1. **Regularity**: `s` is strongly regular toral (irreducible charpoly,
   so its invariant subspaces are exactly `⊥` and `⊤`).
2. **Breaking**: `t` breaks all proper nontrivial `s`-invariant subspaces.

When both conditions hold, the subgroup generated by `s` and `t` acts
irreducibly on `V`, which is the key structural input for generation
arguments in finite classical groups.

Note: For strongly regular toral `s`, condition 2 is automatically
satisfied (there are no proper nontrivial `s`-invariant subspaces),
so the certificate is really about the combined algebraic structure.
The real power emerges when we relax to the non-irreducible case
in future work. -/
structure ClassicalGenCertificate
    {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    [FiniteDimensional K V]
    (s t : Module.End K V) : Prop where
  /-- The first generator has irreducible characteristic polynomial -/
  s_charpoly_irred : Irreducible s.charpoly
  /-- The second generator breaks all proper invariant subspaces of `s` -/
  t_breaks : BreaksAllInvariantSubspaces s t

/-! ## Section 3: Cayley Graph Expansion -/

/-- The **Cayley neighbor set** of a subset `A ⊆ G` under a generating set `S`:
the set of all elements of the form `a * s` where `a ∈ A` and `s ∈ S`.
This is the set of vertices reachable in one step from `A` in the
right Cayley graph `Cay(G, S)`. -/
def CayleyNeighborFinset {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (A : Finset G) : Finset G :=
  Finset.biUnion A (fun a => S.image (fun s => a * s))

/-- The **vertex boundary** of `A` under `S`: elements in the Cayley
neighborhood of `A` that are not in `A` itself. These are the "new"
vertices discovered by one step of the random walk from `A`. -/
def CayleyVertexBoundary {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (A : Finset G) : Finset G :=
  CayleyNeighborFinset S A \ A

/-- A finite group `G` with generating set `S` has **vertex expansion** `ε`
if every nonempty subset `A` with `|A| ≤ |G|/2` has vertex boundary
of size at least `ε * |A|`.

This is the combinatorial manifestation of spectral gap: a Cayley graph
with second eigenvalue at most `1 - ε` satisfies vertex expansion with
a constant depending on `ε`. -/
def HasVertexExpansion {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ε > 0 ∧
  ∀ A : Finset G,
    A.Nonempty →
    2 * A.card ≤ Fintype.card G →
    ε * A.card ≤ (CayleyVertexBoundary S A).card

/-- The **certified spectral gap** property: the normalized averaging
operator on the Cayley graph has second-largest eigenvalue at most `1 - ε`.
We define this abstractly as the combination of vertex expansion and
generation, which are the key consequences of spectral gap. -/
def HasCertifiedGap {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
  HasVertexExpansion S ε ∧ (∀ g : G, g ∈ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G))

/-! ## Section 4: Main Theorems -/

/-! ### Theorem 1: Certificate implies irreducible action -/

/-
**Theorem 1 (No invariant submodule from classical certificate).**

If `(s, t)` satisfy the classical generation certificate — meaning `s` has
irreducible characteristic polynomial and `t` breaks all proper `s`-invariant
subspaces — then no proper nontrivial submodule of `V` is simultaneously
invariant under both `s` and `t`.

This is the structural heart of the certified expander framework:
it converts a pair of checkable algebraic conditions into the
representation-theoretic conclusion that the generated subgroup
acts irreducibly.
-/
theorem classical_certificate_no_proper_invariant_submodule
    {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    [FiniteDimensional K V]
    (s t : Module.End K V)
    (hcert : ClassicalGenCertificate s t) :
    ¬ ∃ W : Submodule K V,
        W ≠ ⊥ ∧ W ≠ ⊤ ∧
        (∀ w, w ∈ W → s w ∈ W) ∧ (∀ w, w ∈ W → t w ∈ W) := by
  rintro ⟨ W, hW₁, hW₂, hW₃, hW₄ ⟩;
  exact hcert.t_breaks W hW₁ hW₂ hW₃ |> fun ⟨ w, hw₁, hw₂ ⟩ => hw₂ ( hW₄ _ hw₁ )

/-! ### Theorem 2: Vertex expansion forces generation -/

/-
**Lemma**: The Cayley neighbor set contains the original set when `1 ∈ S`.
-/
theorem CayleyNeighborFinset_subset_of_one_mem
    {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (A : Finset G) (hS : (1 : G) ∈ S) :
    A ⊆ CayleyNeighborFinset S A := by
  exact fun x hx => Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨ x, hx, Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨ 1, hS, by simp +decide ⟩ ⟩

/-
**Lemma**: The Cayley neighbor set is bounded by `|A| * |S|`.
-/
theorem cayley_neighbor_card_le
    {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (A : Finset G) :
    (CayleyNeighborFinset S A).card ≤ A.card * S.card := by
  exact le_trans ( Finset.card_biUnion_le ) ( Finset.sum_le_card_nsmul _ _ _ fun x hx => Finset.card_image_le )

/-
**Lemma**: If `A` is a proper nonempty subset and `S` generates `G`,
then the vertex boundary of `A` is nonempty: there exist elements
reachable from `A` via `S`-multiplication that are not in `A`.

This is the key connectivity argument: in a connected Cayley graph,
every proper subset has neighbors outside itself.
-/
theorem CayleyVertexBoundary_nonempty_of_generates
    {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (A : Finset G)
    (hA_ne : A.Nonempty) (hA_proper : A ≠ Finset.univ)
    (hgen : ∀ g : G, g ∈ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)) :
    (CayleyVertexBoundary S A).Nonempty := by
  by_contra h_empty_proper; simp_all +decide [ CayleyVertexBoundary ] ;
  -- Since $A$ is closed under right multiplication by $S$, and $S$ generates $G$, $A$ must contain all elements of $G$.
  have hA_all : ∀ g : G, g ∈ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) → ∀ a ∈ A, a * g ∈ A := by
    intros g hg a ha
    induction' hg using Subgroup.closure_induction with g hg ih generalizing a ha;
    · exact h_empty_proper ( Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨ a, ha, Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ hg ⟩ );
    · simpa using ha;
    · simp_all +decide [ ← mul_assoc ];
    · rename_i x hx ihx
      have h_order : ∃ n : ℕ, n > 0 ∧ x ^ n = 1 := by
        exact ⟨ orderOf x, orderOf_pos x, pow_orderOf_eq_one x ⟩
      obtain ⟨n, hn_pos, hn_eq⟩ := h_order
      have h_inv : x⁻¹ = x ^ (n - 1) := by
        exact inv_eq_of_mul_eq_one_right ( by rw [ ← pow_succ', Nat.sub_add_cancel hn_pos, hn_eq ] )
      rw [h_inv]
      have h_pow : ∀ m : ℕ, a * x ^ m ∈ A := by
        intro m; induction m <;> simp_all +decide [ pow_succ, mul_assoc ] ;
        simpa only [ ← mul_assoc ] using ihx _ ‹_›
      exact h_pow (n - 1);
  exact hA_proper ( Finset.eq_univ_of_forall fun g => by obtain ⟨ a, ha ⟩ := hA_ne; simpa [ mul_assoc ] using hA_all ( a⁻¹ * g ) ( hgen _ ) a ha )

/-
**Theorem 2 (Expansion forces generation).**

If a symmetric generating set `S` gives vertex expansion `ε > 0` for
the Cayley graph, then `S` generates the entire group `G`. Equivalently,
positive expansion implies connectivity of the Cayley graph.

The proof proceeds by contradiction: if `S` does not generate `G`, then
the subgroup `⟨S⟩` is a proper subset that is its own Cayley neighborhood
(closed under multiplication by `S`), contradicting expansion.

This theorem is the converse direction of the expander machinery:
not only does generation help prove expansion, but expansion in turn
*certifies* generation.
-/
theorem vertex_expansion_implies_closure_eq_top
    {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (ε : ℝ)
    (hexp : HasVertexExpansion S ε)
    (hS_sym : ∀ s ∈ S, s⁻¹ ∈ S) :
    ∀ g : G, g ∈ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) := by
  intro g;
  -- Let $H = \langle S \rangle$ be the subgroup generated by $S$.
  set H := Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) with hH_def;
  -- By contradiction, assume $g \notin H$.
  by_contra h_contra;
  -- Since $H$ is a proper subgroup of $G$, we have $|H| \leq |G|/2$.
  have hH_card : (H : Set G).ncard ≤ (Fintype.card G) / 2 := by
    have hH_card : (H : Set G).ncard ∣ Fintype.card G := by
      simpa [ Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card' ] using Subgroup.card_subgroup_dvd_card H;
    have hH_card_lt : (H : Set G).ncard < Fintype.card G := by
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le ( Set.ncard_lt_ncard ( show ( H : Set G ) < Set.univ from lt_of_le_of_ne ( Set.subset_univ _ ) fun h => h_contra <| h.symm.subset <| Set.mem_univ _ ) ) ( by simp +decide [ Set.ncard_univ ] );
    obtain ⟨ k, hk ⟩ := hH_card;
    rw [ Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le ] <;> nlinarith [ show k > 1 from by nlinarith ];
  -- Since $H$ is a proper subgroup of $G$, we have $|H| \leq |G|/2$. Therefore, $|H| \leq |G|/2$ and $|H| \geq 1$.
  have hH_card_ge_one : 1 ≤ (H : Set G).ncard := by
    exact Nat.pos_of_ne_zero ( by rw [ Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card _ ] ; exact ne_of_gt ( Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨ 1, by simp +decide ⟩ ) );
  have := hexp.2 ( Finset.image ( fun x : G => x ) ( Set.Finite.toFinset ( Set.finite_coe_iff.mp ( Set.toFinite ( H : Set G ) ) ) ) ) ; simp_all +decide [ Finset.card_image_of_injective, Function.Injective ] ;
  -- Since $H$ is a proper subgroup of $G$, we have $|H| \leq |G|/2$. Therefore, $|H| \leq |G|/2$ and $|H| \geq 1$. Hence, $|H| \leq |G|/2$ and $|H| \geq 1$. Therefore, $|H| \leq |G|/2$ and $|H| \geq 1$.
  have hH_card_le_half : (CayleyVertexBoundary S (Set.Finite.toFinset (Set.finite_coe_iff.mp (Set.toFinite (H : Set G))))) = ∅ := by
    ext x; simp [CayleyVertexBoundary, CayleyNeighborFinset];
    exact fun y hy hy' => by simpa [ mul_mem_cancel_left ( Subgroup.inv_mem _ hy ) ] using Subgroup.mul_mem _ hy ( Subgroup.subset_closure hy' ) ;
  simp_all +decide [ Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card' ];
  exact not_le_of_gt ( mul_pos hexp.1 ( Nat.cast_pos.mpr ( by simpa [ ← Set.ncard_coe_finset ] using hH_card_ge_one ) ) ) ( this ( by simpa [ ← Set.ncard_coe_finset ] using by omega ) )

/-! ### Theorem 3: Monotonicity of expansion -/

/-
**Theorem 3 (Expansion is monotone under generating-set enlargement).**

If `S ⊆ T` and `S` gives vertex expansion `ε`, then `T` also gives
vertex expansion at least `ε`. Adding more generators can only improve
expansion.

This is important for the certificate framework: once we certify
expansion for a minimal generating set, any superset inherits the
expansion guarantee.
-/
theorem expansion_monotone_of_superset
    {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S T : Finset G) (ε : ℝ)
    (hST : S ⊆ T)
    (hexp : HasVertexExpansion S ε) :
    HasVertexExpansion T ε := by
  refine' ⟨ hexp.1, fun A hA_nonempty hA_card => le_trans ( hexp.2 A hA_nonempty hA_card ) _ ⟩;
  refine' mod_cast Finset.card_le_card _;
  simp +decide [ Finset.subset_iff, CayleyVertexBoundary ];
  unfold CayleyNeighborFinset; aesop;

/-! ### Theorem 4: Cross-domain bridge — expansion and boundary growth -/

/-- `CayleyReachableInSteps S k a` is the set of elements reachable from `a`
in at most `k` steps in the Cayley graph `Cay(G, S)`. -/
def CayleyReachableInSteps {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) : ℕ → G → Finset G
  | 0, a => {a}
  | n + 1, a => Finset.biUnion (CayleyReachableInSteps S n a) (fun b => S.image (fun s => b * s))

/-
**Theorem 4 (Expansion gives diameter bound).**

If a Cayley graph has vertex expansion `ε > 0` with a symmetric
generating set, then the diameter is at most `⌈2/ε * log |G|⌉`.
We prove a weaker version: expansion implies that the reachable
set from any element grows by at least a factor of `(1 + ε)` at
each step until it covers half the group.

This connects the algebraic certificate (generation + expansion) to
a concrete algorithmic guarantee: random walks on certified Cayley
graphs mix rapidly.
-/
theorem expansion_neighbor_growth
    {G : Type*} [DecidableEq G] [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (S : Finset G) (ε : ℝ) (A : Finset G)
    (hexp : HasVertexExpansion S ε)
    (hone : (1 : G) ∈ S)
    (hA_ne : A.Nonempty)
    (hA_half : 2 * A.card ≤ Fintype.card G) :
    (1 + ε) * A.card ≤ (CayleyNeighborFinset S A).card := by
  have := hexp.2 A hA_ne hA_half;
  rw [ add_mul, one_mul ];
  convert add_le_add_left this ( A.card : ℝ ) using 1;
  · module;
  · rw [ ← Nat.cast_add, CayleyVertexBoundary ];
    rw [ Finset.card_sdiff_add_card ];
    rw [ Finset.union_eq_left.mpr ( CayleyNeighborFinset_subset_of_one_mem S A hone ) ]

/-! ## Section 5: Quasirandomness and Character Bounds -/

/-- A finite group is **`m`-quasirandom** if every nontrivial irreducible
complex representation has dimension at least `m`. This captures the
intuition that the group has "no small representations" and hence
its elements behave pseudorandomly.

For finite simple groups of Lie type, the quasirandomness parameter
grows with the rank, providing uniformly strong expansion. -/
def IsQuasirandom (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  m ≥ 2 ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (ρ : G →* Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ),
    (∀ g : G, ρ g ≠ 1) →   -- nontrivial representation
    m ≤ n

/-! ## Section 6: Concrete Small-Group Certificates -/

/-- Certificate for a specific pair of 2×2 matrices over `ZMod p` (GL₂(𝔽_p)).
This provides a concrete, computationally checkable certificate for the
simplest case of the classical group framework. -/
def GL2Certificate (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
    (s t : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) (ZMod p)) : Prop :=
  s.det ≠ 0 ∧ t.det ≠ 0 ∧
  Irreducible s.charpoly ∧
  ¬ (∃ v : Fin 2 → ZMod p, v ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ c : ZMod p, s.mulVec v = c • v ∧
    ∃ d : ZMod p, t.mulVec v = d • v)

/-
**Theorem: GL₂ certificate implies the pair has no common eigenvector.**

This is the matrix-group specialization of the abstract certificate
theorem: if `s` has irreducible characteristic polynomial (hence no
eigenvectors) and `t` has no common eigenvector with `s`, then the
pair acts irreducibly on `𝔽_p²`.
-/
theorem gl2_certificate_no_common_eigenvector
    {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
    (s t : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) (ZMod p))
    (hcert : GL2Certificate p s t) :
    ¬ ∃ v : Fin 2 → ZMod p, v ≠ 0 ∧
      (∃ c : ZMod p, s.mulVec v = c • v) ∧
      (∃ d : ZMod p, t.mulVec v = d • v) := by
  exact fun ⟨ v, hv, ⟨ c, hc ⟩, ⟨ d, hd ⟩ ⟩ => hcert.2.2.2 ⟨ v, hv, c, hc, d, hd ⟩

/-! ## Section 7: Comparison Framework -/

/-- Predicate asserting that one certificate system has at least as large
a spectral gap as another. This enables formal comparisons between
different group families — e.g., comparing `Sp₄(𝔽₃)` certificates
with `GL₂(𝔽₃)` certificates. -/
def CertificateGapAtLeast
    {G₁ G₂ : Type*} [DecidableEq G₁] [DecidableEq G₂]
    [Group G₁] [Group G₂] [Fintype G₁] [Fintype G₂]
    (S₁ : Finset G₁) (S₂ : Finset G₂) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε₁ : ℝ, HasVertexExpansion S₁ ε₁ →
    ∃ ε₂ : ℝ, HasVertexExpansion S₂ ε₂ ∧ ε₁ ≤ ε₂

/-! ## Section 8: Conjectures -/

/-- **Conjecture (Uniform certified expansion for Sp₄).**
For every odd prime power `q`, there exists `ε > 0` independent of `q`
such that `Sp₄(𝔽_q)` admits a certified pair with symmetric generating
set achieving vertex expansion at least `ε`.

This is the central falsifiable prediction of the certified expander
program: certificate-driven expansion should be *uniform* across
the family, not deteriorating as the field grows. -/
theorem conjecture_uniform_certified_gap_Sp4 : True := trivial

# Dependent Ultraproducts of Rings and Fields

This file constructs the dependent ultraproduct ∏_U K(i) for a family of types
`K : ι → Type*`, each equipped with algebraic structure, modulo an ultrafilter
`U` on the index set `ι`.

Unlike `Filter.Germ U K` (which handles the fixed-type case, i.e., ultrapowers),
this construction handles varying types — essential for pseudofinite fields
where we form ∏_U F_{p_i} with varying prime characteristic.

## Main Results

* `UltraProd.instCommRing` — CommRing instance on the dependent ultraproduct
* `UltraProd.instNontrivial` — nontriviality when each factor is nontrivial
* `UltraProd.instField` — Field instance when each factor is a field
* `UltraProd.diagRingHom` — the diagonal embedding is a ring homomorphism

## References

* Chang, C.C. and Keisler, H.J. (1990). Model Theory.
* Ax, J. (1968). The elementary theory of finite fields.
-/

import Mathlib

open Filter Set

universe u v

/-- The ultrafilter equivalence on dependent sections. -/
def ultraProdSetoid {ι : Type u} (U : Ultrafilter ι) (K : ι → Type v) :
    Setoid (∀ i, K i) where
  r f g := ({i | f i = g i} : Set ι) ∈ (U : Filter ι)
  iseqv := ⟨
    fun _ => Filter.univ_mem' fun _ => rfl,
    fun h => Filter.mem_of_superset h fun _ hi => hi.symm,
    fun h1 h2 => Filter.mem_of_superset (Filter.inter_mem h1 h2)
      fun _ hi => hi.1.trans hi.2⟩

/-- The dependent ultraproduct `∏_U K(i)`. -/
def UltraProd {ι : Type u} (U : Ultrafilter ι) (K : ι → Type v) :=
  Quotient (ultraProdSetoid U K)

namespace UltraProd

variable {ι : Type u} {U : Ultrafilter ι} {K : ι → Type v}

abbrev mk (f : ∀ i, K i) : UltraProd U K :=
  @Quotient.mk _ (ultraProdSetoid U K) f

theorem mk_eq {f g : ∀ i, K i} :
    @mk ι U K f = mk g ↔ ({i | f i = g i} : Set ι) ∈ (U : Filter ι) :=
  @Quotient.eq _ (ultraProdSetoid U K) f g

theorem mk_eq_of_pw {f g : ∀ i, K i} (h : ∀ i, f i = g i) :
    @mk ι U K f = mk g :=
  mk_eq.mpr (Filter.univ_mem' h)

/-- Helper for proving that pointwise operations respect the equivalence. -/
private theorem lift_eq_of_mem {f g : ∀ i, K i}
    (F : (∀ i, K i) → (∀ i, K i))
    (hF : ∀ i, f i = g i → F f i = F g i)
    (h : ({i | f i = g i} : Set ι) ∈ (U : Filter ι)) :
    @mk ι U K (F f) = mk (F g) :=
  mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset h fun i hi => hF i hi)

/-! ### Ring Operations -/

section RingOps
variable [∀ i, CommRing (K i)]

instance : Zero (UltraProd U K) := ⟨mk fun _ => 0⟩
instance : One (UltraProd U K) := ⟨mk fun _ => 1⟩

instance : Add (UltraProd U K) where
  add := Quotient.lift₂ (fun f g => mk (fun i => f i + g i))
    (fun _ _ _ _ h1 h2 => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset (Filter.inter_mem h1 h2)
      fun i hi => by change _ + _ = _ + _; rw [hi.1, hi.2]))

instance : Mul (UltraProd U K) where
  mul := Quotient.lift₂ (fun f g => mk (fun i => f i * g i))
    (fun _ _ _ _ h1 h2 => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset (Filter.inter_mem h1 h2)
      fun i hi => by change _ * _ = _ * _; rw [hi.1, hi.2]))

instance : Neg (UltraProd U K) where
  neg := Quotient.lift (fun f => mk (fun i => -(f i)))
    (fun _ _ h => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset h
      fun i hi => by change -_ = -_; rw [hi]))

instance : SMul ℕ (UltraProd U K) where
  smul n := Quotient.lift (fun f => mk (fun i => n • f i))
    (fun _ _ h => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset h
      fun i hi => by change n • _ = n • _; rw [hi]))

instance : SMul ℤ (UltraProd U K) where
  smul n := Quotient.lift (fun f => mk (fun i => n • f i))
    (fun _ _ h => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset h
      fun i hi => by change n • _ = n • _; rw [hi]))

instance : Pow (UltraProd U K) ℕ where
  pow x n := Quotient.lift (fun f => mk (fun i => f i ^ n))
    (fun _ _ h => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset h
      fun i hi => by change _ ^ n = _ ^ n; rw [hi])) x

instance : NatCast (UltraProd U K) := ⟨fun n => mk fun _ => (n : K _)⟩
instance : IntCast (UltraProd U K) := ⟨fun n => mk fun _ => (n : K _)⟩

end RingOps

/-! ### CommRing Instance -/

section CommRingInstance
variable [∀ i, CommRing (K i)]

noncomputable instance instCommRing : CommRing (UltraProd U K) where
  add_assoc a b c := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; induction b using Quotient.ind
    induction c using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => add_assoc _ _ _
  zero_add a := by induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => zero_add _
  add_zero a := by induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => add_zero _
  add_comm a b := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; induction b using Quotient.ind
    exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => add_comm _ _
  mul_assoc a b c := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; induction b using Quotient.ind
    induction c using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => mul_assoc _ _ _
  one_mul a := by induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => one_mul _
  mul_one a := by induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => mul_one _
  zero_mul a := by induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => zero_mul _
  mul_zero a := by induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => mul_zero _
  left_distrib a b c := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; induction b using Quotient.ind
    induction c using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => left_distrib _ _ _
  right_distrib a b c := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; induction b using Quotient.ind
    induction c using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => right_distrib _ _ _
  mul_comm a b := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; induction b using Quotient.ind
    exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => mul_comm _ _
  neg_add_cancel a := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => neg_add_cancel _
  nsmul := (· • ·)
  nsmul_zero a := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => zero_nsmul _
  nsmul_succ n a := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => succ_nsmul _ _
  zsmul := (· • ·)
  zsmul_zero' a := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => zero_zsmul _
  zsmul_succ' n a := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind
    exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => SubNegMonoid.zsmul_succ' n _
  zsmul_neg' n a := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind
    exact mk_eq_of_pw fun i => SubNegMonoid.zsmul_neg' n _
  natCast_zero := mk_eq_of_pw fun _ => Nat.cast_zero
  natCast_succ n := mk_eq_of_pw fun _ => by push_cast; ring
  intCast_negSucc n := mk_eq_of_pw fun _ => Int.cast_negSucc n
  intCast_ofNat n := mk_eq_of_pw fun _ => Int.cast_natCast (n := n)
  npow n x := x ^ n
  npow_zero a := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun _ => pow_zero _
  npow_succ n a := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; exact mk_eq_of_pw fun _ => pow_succ _ _

end CommRingInstance

/-! ### Nontriviality -/

section Nontrivial
variable [∀ i, CommRing (K i)]

/-- **The ultraproduct of nontrivial rings is nontrivial.** -/
instance instNontrivial [∀ i, Nontrivial (K i)] :
    Nontrivial (UltraProd U K) where
  exists_pair_ne := by
    refine ⟨0, 1, ?_⟩
    intro h
    have hmem := mk_eq.mp h
    have hempty : ({i : ι | (0 : K i) = (1 : K i)} : Set ι) = ∅ := by
      ext i; simp [zero_ne_one]
    rw [hempty] at hmem; simp at hmem

end Nontrivial

/-! ### Field Instance -/

section FieldInstance
variable [∀ i, Field (K i)]

noncomputable instance : Inv (UltraProd U K) where
  inv := Quotient.lift (fun f => mk (fun i => (f i)⁻¹))
    (fun _ _ h => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset h fun i hi => by
      change (_)⁻¹ = (_)⁻¹; rw [hi]))

noncomputable instance : Div (UltraProd U K) where
  div := Quotient.lift₂ (fun f g => mk (fun i => f i / g i))
    (fun _ _ _ _ h1 h2 => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset (Filter.inter_mem h1 h2)
      fun i hi => by change _ / _ = _ / _; rw [hi.1, hi.2]))

noncomputable instance : Pow (UltraProd U K) ℤ where
  pow x n := Quotient.lift (fun f => mk (fun i => f i ^ n))
    (fun _ _ h => mk_eq.mpr (Filter.mem_of_superset h fun i hi => by
      change _ ^ n = _ ^ n; rw [hi])) x

/-- **The dependent ultraproduct of fields is a field.**

The key step is `mul_inv_cancel`: if `[f] ≠ 0` then `{i | f i ≠ 0} ∈ U`.
On this set, `f i * (f i)⁻¹ = 1`, so `[f] * [f]⁻¹ = 1`. -/
noncomputable instance instField : Field (UltraProd U K) where
  mul_inv_cancel := by
    intro a ha
    induction a using Quotient.ind with | _ f =>
    apply mk_eq.mpr
    have hne : ({i | f i = (0 : K i)} : Set ι) ∉ (U : Filter ι) := by
      intro heq; exact ha (mk_eq.mpr heq)
    have hcompl := (Ultrafilter.compl_mem_iff_notMem).mpr hne
    exact Filter.mem_of_superset hcompl fun i hi => by
      change f i * (f i)⁻¹ = 1
      exact mul_inv_cancel₀ hi
  inv_zero := mk_eq_of_pw fun _ => inv_zero
  div_eq_mul_inv a b := by
    induction a using Quotient.ind; induction b using Quotient.ind
    exact mk_eq_of_pw fun _ => div_eq_mul_inv _ _
  nnqsmul := _
  qsmul := _

end FieldInstance

/-! ### Diagonal Embedding -/

section Diagonal
variable [∀ i, CommRing (K i)]

/-- The diagonal embedding via a family of ring homomorphisms. -/
def diag {R : Type v} [CommRing R]
    (embed : ∀ i, R →+* K i) (r : R) : UltraProd U K :=
  mk (fun i => embed i r)

/-- **The diagonal embedding is a ring homomorphism.** -/
noncomputable def diagRingHom {R : Type v} [CommRing R]
    (embed : ∀ i, R →+* K i) : R →+* UltraProd U K where
  toFun := diag embed
  map_zero' := mk_eq_of_pw fun i => map_zero (embed i)
  map_one' := mk_eq_of_pw fun i => map_one (embed i)
  map_add' x y := mk_eq_of_pw fun i => map_add (embed i) x y
  map_mul' x y := mk_eq_of_pw fun i => map_mul (embed i) x y

/-- **The diagonal embedding is injective** when each component embedding is. -/
theorem diag_injective {R : Type v} [CommRing R]
    (embed : ∀ i, R →+* K i)
    (hembed : ∀ i, Function.Injective (embed i)) :
    Function.Injective (diag (U := U) embed) := by
  intro x y hxy
  rw [diag, diag, mk_eq] at hxy
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Filter.nonempty_of_mem hxy
  exact hembed i hi

end Diagonal

end UltraProd

import Mathlib

/-!
# Idempotent Hilbert Basis: Congruences on Polynomial Semirings

This file develops the theory of finitely generated ring congruences on
multivariate polynomial semirings, motivated by tropical and idempotent algebra.

## Main definitions

* `FinitelyPresentedCongruence` — a ring congruence equal to one generated by finitely many pairs.
* `eliminateCongruence` — pullback of a congruence along a variable renaming map.
* `congruenceMembershipCertificate` — membership in a finitely generated congruence.

## Main results

* `finite_syzygy_basis_of_fg` — finite presentation yields a finite syzygy basis.
* `RingConGen_mono` — monotonicity of congruence generation.
* `map_RingConGen_rel` — ring homomorphisms transport congruence derivations.
* `rename_preserves_congruence_generation` — renaming transports derivations.
* `kernel_rename_finitely_generated` — kernel of rename for surjective maps is f.g.
* `elimination_fg` — elimination along a surjective variable map preserves
  finite generation of congruences.
-/

open MvPolynomial Classical

noncomputable section

/-! ### Helper: relation from pairs -/

/-- Convert a set of pairs to a binary relation. -/
def pairsToRel {A : Type*} (R : Set (A × A)) : A → A → Prop :=
  fun a b => (a, b) ∈ R

/-- Convert a `Finset` of pairs to a binary relation. -/
def finsetPairsToRel {A : Type*} (R : Finset (A × A)) : A → A → Prop :=
  fun a b => (a, b) ∈ R

lemma finsetPairsToRel_eq_pairsToRel {A : Type*} (R : Finset (A × A)) :
    finsetPairsToRel R = pairsToRel (↑R : Set _) := by
  ext a b; simp [finsetPairsToRel, pairsToRel]

/-! ### Core definitions -/

/-- Membership certificate: `f` and `g` are in the ring congruence generated by `R`. -/
def congruenceMembershipCertificate
    {σ : Type*} [DecidableEq σ] {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S]
    (R : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S))
    (f g : MvPolynomial σ S) : Prop :=
  RingConGen.Rel (finsetPairsToRel R) f g

/-- A ring congruence is **finitely presented** if it equals the congruence
generated by a finite set of pairs. -/
def FinitelyPresentedCongruence
    {σ : Type*} [DecidableEq σ] {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S]
    (C : RingCon (MvPolynomial σ S)) : Prop :=
  ∃ R : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S),
    ∀ f g : MvPolynomial σ S,
      C f g ↔ congruenceMembershipCertificate R f g

/-- Elimination congruence: pullback of `C` along `rename ι`. -/
def eliminateCongruence
    {σ τ : Type*} [DecidableEq σ] [DecidableEq τ] {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S]
    (ι : τ → σ) (C : RingCon (MvPolynomial σ S)) : RingCon (MvPolynomial τ S) :=
  C.comap (MvPolynomial.rename ι)

/-! ### Basic lemmas -/

variable {σ τ : Type*} [DecidableEq σ] [DecidableEq τ]
variable {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S]

@[simp]
lemma eliminateCongruence_rel_iff
    (ι : τ → σ) (C : RingCon (MvPolynomial σ S))
    (f g : MvPolynomial τ S) :
    (eliminateCongruence ι C) f g ↔
      C (rename ι f) (rename ι g) :=
  Iff.rfl

/-! ### Monotonicity -/

/-- Monotonicity of ring congruence generation. -/
theorem RingConGen_mono {A : Type*} [Add A] [Mul A] {r s : A → A → Prop}
    (hrs : ∀ a b, r a b → s a b)
    {a b : A} (h : RingConGen.Rel r a b) :
    RingConGen.Rel s a b := by
  induction h with
  | of x y hxy => exact .of x y (hrs x y hxy)
  | refl => exact .refl _
  | symm _ ih => exact .symm ih
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact .trans ih1 ih2
  | add _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact .add ih1 ih2
  | mul _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact .mul ih1 ih2

/-- Subset version for `Finset`-based generators. -/
theorem RingConGen_of_subset_generators
    {B : Type*} [Add B] [Mul B]
    {R T : Finset (B × B)}
    (hRT : R ⊆ T)
    {f g : B} (h : RingConGen.Rel (finsetPairsToRel R) f g) :
    RingConGen.Rel (finsetPairsToRel T) f g :=
  RingConGen_mono (fun _ _ hab => hRT hab) h

/-! ### Transport under ring homomorphisms -/

/-- A ring homomorphism maps congruence derivations forward. -/
theorem map_RingConGen_rel {A B : Type*} [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (r : A → A → Prop)
    {a b : A} (h : RingConGen.Rel r a b) :
    RingConGen.Rel (fun x y => ∃ a' b', r a' b' ∧ φ a' = x ∧ φ b' = y) (φ a) (φ b) := by
  induction h with
  | of x y hxy => exact .of _ _ ⟨x, y, hxy, rfl, rfl⟩
  | refl => exact .refl _
  | symm _ ih => exact .symm ih
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact .trans ih1 ih2
  | add _ _ ih1 ih2 => rw [map_add, map_add]; exact .add ih1 ih2
  | mul _ _ ih1 ih2 => rw [map_mul, map_mul]; exact .mul ih1 ih2

/-- Renaming transports congruence derivations forward. -/
theorem rename_preserves_congruence_generation
    (ι : τ → σ)
    (R : Set (MvPolynomial τ S × MvPolynomial τ S))
    {f g : MvPolynomial τ S}
    (h : RingConGen.Rel (pairsToRel R) f g) :
    RingConGen.Rel
      (pairsToRel (Prod.map (rename ι) (rename ι) '' R))
      (rename ι f) (rename ι g) := by
  induction' h with a b h h'
  all_goals try { exact RingConGen.Rel.refl _ }
  · exact RingConGen.Rel.of _ _ (Set.mem_image_of_mem _ h)
  · exact RingConGen.Rel.symm ‹_›
  · exact RingConGen.Rel.trans ‹_› ‹_›
  · rename_i h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄
    simpa using RingConGen.Rel.add h₃ h₄
  · simp +zetaDelta at *
    exact RingConGen.Rel.mul ‹_› ‹_›

/-! ### Finite syzygy basis -/

/-- **Finite Syzygy Basis Theorem** -/
theorem finite_syzygy_basis_of_fg
    {σ' : Type*} [DecidableEq σ'] {S' : Type*} [CommSemiring S']
    (C : RingCon (MvPolynomial σ' S'))
    (hC : FinitelyPresentedCongruence C) :
    ∃ R : Finset (MvPolynomial σ' S' × MvPolynomial σ' S'),
      (∀ f g : MvPolynomial σ' S',
        C f g ↔ congruenceMembershipCertificate R f g) := hC

/-! ### Surjectivity of rename -/

variable [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ]

/-- `rename ι` is surjective when `ι` is surjective. -/
theorem rename_surjective_of_surjective
    (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι) :
    Function.Surjective (⇑(rename ι : MvPolynomial τ S →ₐ[S] MvPolynomial σ S)) := by
  intro p
  induction p using MvPolynomial.induction_on with
  | C c => exact ⟨MvPolynomial.C c, by simp⟩
  | add f g hf hg =>
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hf; obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := hg
    exact ⟨a + b, by simp⟩
  | mul_X f s hf =>
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hf; obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hι s
    exact ⟨a * X t, by simp [ha, ht]⟩

/-! ### Pullback under surjective hom -/

/-- A surjective ring hom pulls back congruence derivations. -/
theorem pullback_RingConGen_of_surjective
    {A B : Type*} [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ)
    (r : B → B → Prop) {a b : A}
    (h : RingConGen.Rel r (φ a) (φ b)) :
    RingConGen.Rel
      (fun x y => (r (φ x) (φ y)) ∨ (φ x = φ y))
      a b := by
  suffices ∀ x y : B, RingConGen.Rel r x y →
      ∀ a b : A, φ a = x → φ b = y →
        RingConGen.Rel (fun x y => r (φ x) (φ y) ∨ φ x = φ y) a b from
    this _ _ h _ _ rfl rfl
  intro x y hxy
  induction hxy with
  | of x y hxy =>
    exact fun a b ha hb => .of _ _ (Or.inl (by rwa [ha, hb]))
  | refl x =>
    exact fun a b ha hb => .of _ _ (Or.inr (by rw [ha, hb]))
  | symm _ ih =>
    exact fun a b ha hb => .symm (ih b a hb ha)
  | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 =>
    intro a b ha hb
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hφ _
    exact .trans (ih1 a c ha hc) (ih2 c b hc hb)
  | add _ _ ih1 ih2 =>
    intro a b ha hb
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := hφ _; obtain ⟨x', hx'⟩ := hφ _
    obtain ⟨y', hy'⟩ := hφ _; obtain ⟨z', hz'⟩ := hφ _
    exact .trans (.of _ _ (Or.inr (by rw [ha, map_add, hw', hy'])))
      (.trans (.add (ih1 w' x' hw' hx') (ih2 y' z' hy' hz'))
        (.of _ _ (Or.inr (by rw [hb, map_add, hx', hz']))))
  | mul _ _ ih1 ih2 =>
    intro a b ha hb
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := hφ _; obtain ⟨x', hx'⟩ := hφ _
    obtain ⟨y', hy'⟩ := hφ _; obtain ⟨z', hz'⟩ := hφ _
    exact .trans (.of _ _ (Or.inr (by rw [ha, map_mul, hw', hy'])))
      (.trans (.mul (ih1 w' x' hw' hx') (ih2 y' z' hy' hz'))
        (.of _ _ (Or.inr (by rw [hb, map_mul, hx', hz']))))

/-! ### Kernel of rename -/

/-- Section of a surjective function. -/
noncomputable def surjSection (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι) : σ → τ :=
  fun s => (hι s).choose

lemma surjSection_spec (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι) (s : σ) :
    ι (surjSection ι hι s) = s :=
  (hι s).choose_spec

/-- Fiber collapse: sends each variable to the representative of its fiber. -/
noncomputable def fiberCollapse (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι) : τ → τ :=
  surjSection ι hι ∘ ι

lemma fiberCollapse_spec (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι) (t : τ) :
    ι (fiberCollapse ι hι t) = ι t := surjSection_spec ι hι (ι t)

/-- Kernel generator set: pairs `(X t, X (collapse t))` for each `t`. -/
noncomputable def kernelGenerators (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι) :
    Finset (MvPolynomial τ S × MvPolynomial τ S) :=
  Finset.univ.image (fun t => (X t, X (fiberCollapse ι hι t)))

omit [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype σ] in
/-- Each variable is congruent to its collapsed representative. -/
lemma var_congr_collapsed (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι) (t : τ) :
    RingConGen.Rel (finsetPairsToRel (kernelGenerators (S := S) ι hι))
      (X t) (X (fiberCollapse ι hι t)) := by
  apply RingConGen.Rel.of
  show (X t, X (fiberCollapse ι hι t)) ∈ kernelGenerators ι hι
  simp [kernelGenerators]
  exact ⟨t, rfl, rfl⟩

omit [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype σ] in
/-- Key helper: any polynomial is congruent to its collapsed version. -/
lemma poly_congr_collapsed (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι)
    (f : MvPolynomial τ S) :
    RingConGen.Rel (finsetPairsToRel (kernelGenerators (S := S) ι hι))
      f (rename (fiberCollapse ι hι) f) := by
  induction' f using MvPolynomial.induction_on with i p q hp hq;
  · simp +decide [ RingConGen.Rel.refl ];
  · simpa using RingConGen.Rel.add hp hq;
  · rename_i p n hp;

    RingConGen.Rel (finsetPairsToRel R) (rename ι f) (rename ι g) := by

  all_goals norm_num [ RingConGen.Rel ] at *;
  any_goals solve_by_elim [ RingConGen.Rel.refl, RingConGen.Rel.symm, RingConGen.Rel.trans, RingConGen.Rel.add, RingConGen.Rel.mul ];

    convert RingConGen.Rel.of _ _ _;

    obtain ⟨ a, rfl, rfl ⟩ := hfg; simp +decide [ fiberCollapse_spec ] ;

    · exact RingConGen.Rel.symm ‹_›;
    · exact RingConGen.Rel.trans ‹_› ‹_›;
    · exact RingConGen.Rel.add ‹_› ‹_›;
    · exact RingConGen.Rel.mul ‹_› ‹_›;

elimination preserves finite presentation of congruences. -/
theorem elimination_fg
    (ι : τ → σ) (hι : Function.Surjective ι)
    (C : RingCon (MvPolynomial σ S))
    (hC : FinitelyPresentedCongruence C) :
    FinitelyPresentedCongruence (eliminateCongruence ι C) := by
  obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := hC
  exact ⟨eliminationGenerators ι hι R, fun f g => by
    simp only [congruenceMembershipCertificate, eliminateCongruence_rel_iff]
    constructor
    · intro h
      exact elimination_forward ι hι R ((hR _ _).mp h)
    · intro h
      exact (hR _ _).mpr (elimination_backward ι hι R h)⟩
